# @circle-fin/onramp-kit

## 1.0.8

### Patch Changes

- CCTPx is now configured for Ink, HyperEVM and World Chain on mainnet and testnet (Ink Testnet, HyperEVM Testnet and World Chain Sepolia). These chains now report CCTPx support, so CCTPx routes to and from them can be used.
- The shared error codes now include `BORROW_PAUSED`.
  This package does not raise it.

## 1.0.7

### Patch Changes

- `Blockchain.Celo_Sepolia` is now in the chain registry, and
  `Blockchain.Celo_Alfajores_Testnet` is deprecated because Celo shut down
  the Alfajores testnet. This package adds no Celo Sepolia routes.
- When a kit error records the error it wraps, error telemetry now includes a
  fixed-format message naming that error. The message holds the error's class
  name and its numeric code when it has one, for example
  `TransactionExecutionError code=4001`. Errors raised by a separately installed adapter or provider package now
  report their code too. Redacted error projections in traces keep an integer
  `code`. The message never contains error text, addresses or amounts. Error
  codes, types and recoverability are unchanged.
- The shared error codes now include `BORROW_LOAN_OPENING_PENDING`,
  `BORROW_LOAN_OPENING_EXPIRED`, and `BORROW_INSUFFICIENT_MARKET_LIQUIDITY`.
  This package does not raise them.
- The SDK no longer retries an error that it marks `FATAL`, even when the error has a network or RPC error code. For example, a read that fails because no wallet is connected now fails on the first attempt.
- Correct the Onramp documentation about server-side webhooks. The README and
  type docs previously told you to reconcile purchases from Circle's server-side
  webhooks, but Onramp Kit does not send webhooks to your server. The new
  "Confirming a purchase" section explains that lifecycle events are browser
  signals for your UI, and that when your app needs a reliable record of a
  completed purchase, you check on-chain that the token arrived at the
  destination wallet.

  The docs now also cover:

  - Sandbox setup: `baseUrl` `https://api-test.circle.com` and `widgetBaseUrl`
    `https://onramp-sandbox.arc.io` with a testnet API key, plus the `frame-src`
    directive for each environment.
  - Event delivery: events reach only the page that embeds the widget or opened
    it as a popup, not a widget URL opened as a top-level page.
  - Deposit payload fields: for card, Apple Pay, and Google Pay, `amount` is the
    fiat amount paid and `orderId` is the Onramp order ID. For bank transfers,
    `amount` is the amount the customer entered and `orderId` is the customer's
    bank-transfer reference, the same across all of their accounts and deposits.
    `transactionHash` appears only on `DEPOSIT_SETTLED`,
    which is best-effort.
  - Bank transfers: a deposit can land on a wallet the customer set up in an
    earlier session, and later transfers into an open account arrive with no
    widget event.

  No runtime behavior changes.

- Chain definitions now list the EURC contract address on World Chain Sepolia, `0xe479EcA5740Ac65d6E1823bea2f1C08Bc14e954F`, matching the token registry.

## 1.0.6

### Patch Changes

- EURC address updates in chain definitions.

  - `WorldChain.eurcAddress` is now set; it was previously `null`.
  - The EURC addresses on Avalanche, Avalanche Fuji, and Base now use EIP-55 checksum casing instead of all lowercase. If you compare these addresses with `===`, compare them case-insensitively instead.
  - EURC can now be looked up by symbol on Avalanche Fuji and Solana Devnet.

## 1.0.5

### Patch Changes

- Arc Testnet calls no longer fail with `HTTP request failed` when no custom RPC is configured. The default Arc Testnet RPC endpoint is now `https://rpc.testnet.arc.io`, replacing the retired `https://rpc.testnet.arc.network/` host. Apps that already pass their own Arc Testnet RPC URL or transport are unaffected.

## 1.0.4

### Patch Changes

- Fix session `metadata` being dropped after a successful create.

  `createSession` now returns `metadata` when the Onramp API echoes it. `metadata` is part of the session returned by `createSession`, so it reaches the browser when you forward the session. The field was typed as `Record<string, unknown>` even though the API only accepts strings. If you annotate the map as `Record<string, unknown>`, retype it as `Record<string, string>`.

## 1.0.3

### Patch Changes

- Stop replacing a validation error with a `TypeError` when the rejected value
  holds a `bigint`.

  Building a validation error serializes the offending value into the message.
  `JSON.stringify` refuses `bigint` and circular structures, so a value that
  carried either — an on-chain read, or a transaction receipt log, both of which
  routinely hold `bigint` fields — threw
  `TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt` from inside the error
  constructor. The real error never surfaced, and callers saw an unrelated crash
  in its place.

  Such values now render with their `bigint` fields as strings, and a value that
  still cannot be serialized renders as `[unserializable object]`. The error's
  `cause.trace.value` is unchanged and still carries the raw value.

## 1.0.2

### Patch Changes

- Remove the unused `destinationWallet` query param from the widget launch URL.

## 1.0.1

### Patch Changes

- Edit README and align package metadata with the other kits.

## 1.0.0

### Major Changes

- # Onramp Kit Initial Release

  Official Circle SDK for embedding the Arc Onramp widget - server-side session creation and client-side widget mounting in a single npm package.

  ## Core Features

  - **Split Server / Client architecture**: the `apiKey` credential stays on your server; only a short-lived `sessionToken` reaches the browser.
  - **Type-safe APIs**: Zod-validated protocol schemas with strict TypeScript support.
  - **Drop-in route handler**: `createSessionRouteHandler` is a Fetch-API-standard `Request -> Response` function that works in Next.js, Express, Hono, Fastify, Cloudflare Workers, and any runtime supporting the Fetch API.
  - **Two widget modes**: embed the onramp as an iframe (`mountIframe`) or open it in a popup (`openWindow`).
  - **Rich event system**: typed lifecycle events (`onDepositSubmitted`, `onDepositSettled`, `onDepositNotCompleted`, `onInitializationError`, `onInitializationSuccess`) with strongly-typed event envelopes.

  ## Server Kit

  Imported via `@circle-fin/onramp-kit/server`. Creates sessions by exchanging your `apiKey` for a per-user `sessionToken`.

  ```typescript
  import {
    createOnrampServerKit,
    createSessionRouteHandler,
  } from "@circle-fin/onramp-kit/server";

  const server = createOnrampServerKit({
    apiKey: process.env.ONRAMP_API_KEY!,
    referrerDomain: "myapp.com",
  });

  // Drop-in route handler (Next.js, Express, Hono, etc.)
  export const POST = createSessionRouteHandler(server);
  ```

  ## Client Kit

  Imported via `@circle-fin/onramp-kit`. Mounts the onramp widget using a session token obtained from your server route.

  ```typescript
  import { createOnrampKit, fetchOnrampSession } from "@circle-fin/onramp-kit";

  const onramp = createOnrampKit();
  const session = await fetchOnrampSession({
    url: "/api/onramp/sessions",
    body: { appUserId: "usr_1", destinationAddress: "0x..." },
  });

  const widget = onramp.mountIframe({
    session,
    container: document.getElementById("onramp")!,
    onDepositSettled: (event) => console.log("Deposit settled", event),
  });

  // Clean up when done
  widget.close();
  ```

  ## Security

  - **`referrerDomain` is server-only**: set at `createOnrampServerKit` construction time, not client-settable. This prevents a client from widening the Transak iframe `frame-ancestors` CSP allowlist.
  - **Compile-time credential enforcement**: `OnrampServerKitOptions` uses an intersection + union type so calling `createOnrampServerKit({})` without an `apiKey` is a type error, not just a runtime one.
  - **Credential naming**: uses `apiKey`, aligned with the swap-kit / app-kit convention.

  ## Use Cases

  - **Fiat on-ramp integration**: let users buy USDC with fiat directly inside your dApp
  - **Wallet top-up flows**: embed one-click funding into wallet UIs
  - **E-commerce checkout**: accept fiat payments that settle as on-chain USDC
  - **Multi-chain funding**: users can fund any supported destination chain without manual bridging
